Now we see meaningful differentiation. Best fits: M7 (-59.34), M8 (-59.24), M6 (-58.95). These are all "unusual" mechanisms:
- M6: catalyst activation (cat => cat*)
- M7: substrate saturation with 2 substrates on catalyst
- M8: pre-equilibrium ligand dissociation to form active catalyst

Next tier: M2 (-56.77) - dimerization
Then most others cluster around -55 to -56.

M14 and M20 are notably worse. M9 also somewhat worse. This experiment (low catalyst) discriminated some of the deactivation mechanisms (M14, M20 fit worse because at low [cat], deactivation would be minimal in reality but their models may not fit).

Leading hypothesis: M6, M7, M8 involve either catalyst activation or unusual kinetic order. M6 and M8 show induction periods. M7 involves 2 substrates on one catalyst.

Discriminating M6/M8 vs M7: M7 predicts substrate-order dependence (2 substrates on catS) - at LOW substrate, M7's rate would be lower than expected (sublinear at low S). M6 and M8 involve catalyst activation, so induction period should be visible early.

Let me test high substrate concentration to probe:
- M7: at high [S], saturation of catS2 pathway - should predict specific saturation shape
- M6, M8: activation kinetics independent of substrate concentration
- M11, M16: substrate-induced deactivation predicts inhibition at high S

High [S] with normal [cat] will distinguish these.
</reflection>
